items.q: Design a pipeline ingesting fundamentals from 50 sources daily, serving batch analytics and a near-real-time dashboard.
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Three layers: (1) Ingestion -- NiFi fetches data and lands raw files in S3, config-driven per source. (2) Processing -- Spark validates types and business rules; invalid records go to dead-letter S3 with alerts; valid records become Parquet partitioned by date. (3) Serving -- Spark batch jobs query processed data for full analytics; pre-aggregated daily rollups feed the dashboard so it does not hit the heavy pipeline on every page load.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Operating in production requires knowing how the runtime or framework handles state, memory allocations, and execution locks under the hood. Failure to account for these mechanics often leads to subtle bugs that only surface under heavy load.

items.q: How do you design so adding source 51 doesn't require a code change?
items.a:

items.q: What is idempotency and why is it essential?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** An idempotent pipeline produces the same result regardless of how many times it runs on the same input. Re-running today's pipeline should not duplicate records. Implement via mode('overwrite') on Parquet partitions, MERGE statements in SQL, date-partitioned output paths. Enables safe reruns -- how you fix bugs without corrupting data.

items.q: You discover a bug corrupting 2% of records for 3 months. What order do you act in?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** (1) Deploy the fix to stop further corruption. (2) Scope the blast radius -- which records, sources, time period, downstream consumers. (3) Communicate proactively before being asked. (4) Plan and execute backfill. Don't do all at once -- stop the bleeding, understand scope, communicate, fix history, in that order.

items.q: How would you version a dataset schema without breaking existing consumers?
items.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Additive (new nullable columns): Parquet handles automatically -- existing readers see null. Breaking changes: new versioned path (v2/) that new consumers opt into while old consumers stay on v1, or a transition period where both field names coexist before deprecating the old one on a communicated timeline. Never break consumers without a migration path.
